newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan central bank issues further T$2 bln in NCDs.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan central bank issues further T$2 bln in NCDs.

text.p: Taiwan's central bank, in an innovation, issued a further T$2 billion in 14-day negotiable certificates of deposit on Friday at the same 6.442 percent yield set through a morning NCD issue of T$3 billion.
In the morning NCD issue, bids ranged between 6.351 and 6.500 percent, resulting in an average yield of 6.442 percent, the central bank said. Demand totalled T$10.7 billion.

The demand-driven, non-bidding afternoon issuance, a first in Taiwan, enabled the central bank to significantly expand to T$5 billion from $3 billion the amount of liquidity it absorbed through the NCD mechanism.
The central has said in recent days that it planned to experiment with new forms of NCD issuance, including such same-day expanded issues.
Central bank officials declined to say why the bank chose this day to try out the new method.

The bank maintains that its NCD issuance is merely a tool for fine-tuning liquidity on a day-to-day basis, denying that it is linked directly to Taiwan's feverish stock market -- which has been siphoning capital from the money market.

Analysts say they believe the stock market has been a key factor behind the central bank's NCD strategy, as NCD issuance has tended to accelerate at times of extremely high stock market turnover or rapid rises in the stock index.
Friday was no exception. The central bank arranged the initial T$3 billion NCD issue on the heels of a dramatic 2.68 percent stock index rise on Thursday.
Even as the Friday morning NCD issue was being executed, the stock index was surging a further 1.83 percent on extremely high turnover of T$208 billion -- far above Thursday's subdued T$151 billion.

For months, the central bank has adopted what it calls a "stable to loose, but not too loose" monetary policy, hoping to foster a broad economic recovery without fuelling inflation or overly speculative investment due to slack liquidity.

Central bank chief Sheu Yuan-dong said last week the bank would not adjust monetary policy merely to cool Taiwan's red-hot stock market, saying such moves were no "cure all" in the face of concerns of overheating.
